Diving procedures.fact: Towing a surface marker buoy – Buoy towed by a scuba diver to indicate position. Deployment of a decompression buoy – Inflatable surface marker buoy deployed from underwater.

Diving procedures.question: Deployment of a decompression buoy – _____ surface marker buoy deployed from underwater
Diving procedures.fact: Dive planning, the pre-dive briefing. and selection, inspection, preparation and pre-dive checking of diving equipment, may be considered diving procedures, as they are essential parts of the normal diving operation, though they are done before entering the water.

Diving procedures.fact: Deployment of a decompression buoy – Inflatable surface marker buoy deployed from underwater. Planned diving activities – These are mostly considered underwater work, with a few exceptions and borderline cases.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine

Diving procedures.fact: Log dive – Recording specific details about the dive in a diver's logbook (paper or electronic database).

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Surface decompression – _____ the water before fully decompressed and recompressing in a chamber to finish the decompression in relative comfort
Diving procedures.fact: Surface decompression – Leaving the water before fully decompressed and recompressing in a chamber to finish the decompression in relative comfort.

Diving procedures.fact: Operation of the wet bell gas panel – In-water tending – Additional management of the diver's umbilical by an in-water tender where necessary.

Diving procedures.fact: Securing the bell for ascent – Stowing of umbilicals on the bell, checks that the bell is clear to be lifted, and report back to surface that the bell and divers are ready to start the ascent.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine
Diving procedures.question: Tending the working diver – _____ of the working diver's umbilical by the bellman

Diving procedures.question: Transfer under pressure – _____ between pressurised vessels without decompression
Diving procedures.fact: Transfer under pressure – Moving between pressurised vessels without decompression.

Diving procedures.fact: Bailout – Switching to emergency breathing gas supply. Bailout to open circuit – Switching to open circuit scuba emergency gas supply.

Diving procedures.fact: Bailout – Switching to emergency breathing gas supply. Bailout to open circuit – Switching to open circuit scuba emergency gas supply.

Diving procedures.fact: Bailout to closed circuit rebreather – Switching to an emergency rebreather gas supply. Switch and isolate regulator in case of freeze – Close off a frozen regulator and switch to an alternative gas supply.

Diving procedures.fact: Recovery from accidental inversion in dry suit – Avoid uncontrolled ascent following unintended flow of gas to the feet of a dry suit. Follow guideline in silt-out – Avoid getting lost under an overhead.

Diving procedures.fact: Emergency ascents – Procedures for reaching the surface in various emergencies. Lost mask ascent – Ascent when the diver's vision is impaired by not having a mask.

Diving procedures.fact: Assisted ascents – Ascents where the diver in distress is assisted by another diver.

Diving procedures.fact: Buoyant ascent – Using positive buoyancy to rise to the surface.

Diving procedures.fact: Lost weights ascent with flare – Mitigation of an incident where the diver cannot neutralise positive buoyancy.

Diving procedures.fact: Controlled buoyant emergency ascent – Fine control of buoyancy to ascend at an acceptably safe rate.

Diving procedures.fact: Ditch weights to establish buoyancy – Removal of some or all ballast weights to establish neutral or positive buoyancy underwater, or to establish positive buoyancy at the surface.

Diving procedures.fact: Respond to heating water malfunction – Manage thermal imbalance due to inappropriate heating water temperature. Respond to dry suit flood – Manage insulation and buoyancy loss due to flooded dry suit.

Diving procedures.fact: Respond to heating water malfunction – Manage thermal imbalance due to inappropriate heating water temperature. Respond to dry suit flood – Manage insulation and buoyancy loss due to flooded dry suit.

Diving procedures.subject: Health & Medicine

Diving procedures.fact: Umbilical changeout – Swapping a problematic umbilical for a replacement under water.
